b06832a969cccf218dbbeb30305250ef5ad8d3c1
Stabilise two more editor tests under load, assert the cron debounce windows, commit the evidence, and keep raw QA bytes out of the formatter

The audit's first round found one default-parallel coverage run still
failing twice under three busy workers, the changed cron test letting a
zero-delay announcement mutation pass, and 22 cited artefacts uncommitted.
The classifier test enters its six fixture strings as pastes; the editor
test observes the public loading phase before the server's checks; the cron
test advances fake time between edits and asserts the earlier announcement
through 349 ms, the restart of the debounce, and the announcement at 350 ms
(the mutation fails it, unchanged production passes). Every cited artefact
is committed with a provenance manifest. .prettierignore excludes raw QA
JSON, YAML and script artefacts so recorded hashes survive formatting, with
QA Markdown still formatted, and docs/15 states the retention rule.

67c8408839d6990f4739257e036e0483a5e0d7d2
Make the heavy web editor tests deterministic under load

Six editor and Settings test groups timed out at the 20-second default under
coverage with busy CPUs, which made every full web run a retry-only pass.
Fixture text now enters as one input edit (pasteInto), dialog cases mount the
real NodeEditorDialog through the public store without the canvas or app
shell (renderNodeEditor), the cron announcement test controls its debounce
clock, and the secret rename is one replacement edit. Four whole-page
integration cases that remount real forms keep their transitions with an
explicit 60-second budget and a comment each. All 1,070 original assertions
remain; three default-parallel coverage runs and one serial run passed
without retries. Measurements under docs/qa/2026-10-22-web-test-stability/.
